Dated this the 7th day of February, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.65/2012 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kalpetta is the appellant herein.

(For the purpose of convenience,
the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).
2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 2.9.2011.

According to the petitioner, on 2.9.2011 at about 11.15 a.m., while he was riding pillion on a motor cycle from Nelliyambalam to Pariyaram, another motor cycle bearing registration No.KL12F 3110 ridden by the 1st respondent in a rash and negligent manner suddenly sewered the vehicle towards left and in the process, it hit against the motorcycle in which the petitioner was travelling and as a result of the accident, the petitioner fell down and sustained serious injuries.
3. The 1st respondent is the driver , the 2 nd respondent is the owner and 2025:KER:16679 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.14,36,000/- limited to Rs.7,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 and documentary evidence Exhibits A1 to A14 series and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,14,359/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.
8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

Heard Smt. Celine Joseph, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
P.G. Ganappan, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10. The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was a carpenter by profession and as such his notional income fixed by the Tribunal at Rs.7500/- is on the lower side.
The learned counsel for the insurer would argue that the income fixed by the tribunal is reasonable.

Relying upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Neetha and Others v. Divisional Manager,
Maharastra State Road Transport Corporation [(2015) 3 SCC 590], the learned counsel for the petitioner would argue that the Hon'ble Supreme Court has fixed the notional income of a carpenter during the year 2011 at Rs.12,000/-.

entities.text:
Neetha and Others v. Divisional Manager,
Maharastra State Road Transport Corporation [(2015) 3 SCC 590]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11. It is true that in the above decision, the Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the notional income of a carpenter is to be taken as Rs.12,000/-, in 2011, in the light of the notification issued by the State of Karnataka under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 .

Since the minimum wage in Kerala will not 2025:KER:16679 be less than that in Karnataka, I am inclined accept the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.12,000/-.
12.
In the accident the petitioner sustained diffuse brain oedma, intra right temporal craneotomy temporal lob 4.5x3x3 cm.
CT scan dated 6.9.2011 shows intraparenchymal hematoma in right temporal lobe now measures 4.5x3.1x3.0 cm with peritoneal oedma, mass effect in the tissue of effacement of adjacent cortical sulci.

13. As per Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by the medical board, the petitioner suffered 25%
permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, has accepted the permanent physical disability of the petitioner as such and hence, I do not find any grounds to disbelieve the same.
Therefore, the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is accepted as 25%, as fixed by the Tribunal.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 25 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v.
Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v.
Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 2025:KER:16679 SCC 121].

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.9,07,200/-.
15. Towards loss of earning, the tribunal has awarded only Rs.45,000/- being the income for 6 months @ Rs.7,500/-.
Since the notional income of the petitioner is re-fixed at Rs.12,000/-, towards loss of earning he is entitled to get a sum of Rs.72,000/- (12000x6months).
16. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs30,000/- and towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.10,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner,
the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.

sentences.text: 17. The petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 52 days.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings', and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.1,00,000/-, and Rs.50,000/- respectively.
18. Towards bystander expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.4,350/- @ Rs.150 for 29 days.
According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, 2025:KER:16679 the petitioner was treated as inpatient for 52 days.
Therefore, towards bystander expenses, a sum of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.
19. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

20. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.11,81,709/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

2 Transportation 4,150/- 4,150/-
 3 Medical Bills 32,359/- 32,359/-
 4 Bystander expenses 4,350/- 10,000/-
 5 Loss of disability 3,82,500/- 9,07,200/-
 6 Pain and sufferings 30,000/- 1,00,000/-
 7 Extra nourishment 5,000/- 5,000/-
 8 Damage to clothing etc. 1,000/- 1,000/-
 9 Loss of amenities 10,000/- 50,000/-
 Total 5,14,359/- 11,81,709/-
 Enhanced Rs.6,67,350/-
21.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No. 3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.11,81,709/- (Rupees eleven lakh eighty 2025:KER:16679 One thousand seven hundred and nine only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 8% per annum from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, with proportionate costs,
within a period of two months from today
On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
